📝 Essay Reviewer

Teacher-controlled, rule-based essay checker · runs fully offline · no student data leaves this computer

How it works: This tool checks for the specific things you tell it to look for (word counts, required words/phrases, transitions, citations, banned words, etc.), highlights them, and turns the results into a letter grade using your rubric. It detects whether the required ingredients are present — it does not judge the quality of the writing or ideas. Use it as a first-pass checker, then apply your own professional judgment.

🔍 Review an Essay

Assignment & Rubric

Letter-grade scale

The tool adds up the points earned from the checks below, divides by the total possible, and turns that percentage into a letter using this scale. Edit the cutoffs to match your gradebook.

Checks (your IF-THEN rules)

Each check is worth points (its weight). If the essay passes the check, it earns those points. Checks marked “highlight only” don’t affect the grade — they just mark things for your eyes.

Add checks in bulk from a rubric:
How the template columns work
One row per check. Columns: name, type, requirement, points, counts, color, pass_comment, fail_comment.
type — one of: word count, paragraph count, sentence count, required phrase, vocabulary, transitions, citations, banned words, run-on.
requirement — depends on type. Use | to separate list items:
 • word/paragraph/sentence count → min:300 or max:5
 • required phrase → any: I will argue | this essay will (or all: …)
 • vocabulary → all: term1 | term2, any: …, or min2: t1 | t2 | t3
 • transitions → min3 (list optional after a :)
 • citations → any: works_cited | quotes | according_to | parenthetical
 • banned words → gonna | wanna | a lot | stuff
 • run-on → max:45 (flag sentences longer than 45 words)
counts — yes = worth points, no = highlight only. color optional (auto-assigned if blank).
Scanning a rubric doc pulls out your category names and point values and drops in a check “shell” for each — you then pick the type and finish the requirement.
